bridge: P05 introduced tests and C03 introduced algorithms. Use the supplied local program and fixed test evidence.
teaching:
### Compare the three approaches

Fuzzing runs a program on many generated or mutated inputs and looks for failures or other signals. It needs an appropriate target, input format, stopping limits and a way to recognise interesting results.

Static analysis examines code without executing each tested input. It can approximate data flows or risky patterns. Approximation can produce both missed issues and warnings that are not real defects.

Symbolic execution represents some inputs as symbols and follows paths under constraints. A solver helps identify values satisfying a path condition. The number of paths and the model of libraries or environment can limit the analysis.

### Define the failure you care about

A crash is one signal. Incorrect permission, resource exhaustion or silently corrupted data may need an explicit property check. Instrumentation and sanitizers can expose errors that ordinary execution hides.

### Investigate a reported case

Reduce an input to the smallest useful example, reproduce it in the authorised local setup and connect it with the violated rule. A tool report is a lead until that connection is clear.

### State the coverage limit

Time spent or cases executed does not prove that every path or behaviour was checked. Record the target version, assumptions and stopping conditions, and combine methods where they answer different questions.

### Make the repair contract explicit

For the repaired reference, use one ASCII digit 1 through 9, a colon, and exactly that many ASCII letters A–Z or a–z. Reject zero-length bodies and other characters. Check the minimum length before reading text[0] or text[1]. str.isalpha accepts more than English ASCII letters; use an explicit alphabet test if the contract requires ASCII. A path constraint is a condition that must be true for execution to reach a selected branch.
explanation: The empty string and "1" reach unchecked indexing. A repair checks shape/length before indexing, validates a single ASCII digit and separator, then validates body length/letters. Decide whether zero-length bodies are allowed: this fixture requires at least one letter, so "0:" rejects.
exercise: Without external tools, trace all seven supplied inputs and classify accepted, expected ValueError or unexpected exception. Write a guarded repair and assert the intended outcomes. Do not launch any evaluation or model inference as part of this exercise.
challenge: Compare two finite input sets: A=["1:a","2:ab"], B=the seven supplied cases. State the extra defects B reveals and a property neither set proves. Write path constraints for the successful n=2 branch.
challenge_solution: B exposes missing length guards. Neither proves all Unicode, resource-limit or future grammar properties. Successful n=2 requires adequate length, first digit 2, colon at index 1, exactly 2 body characters and the stated alphabet rule. Define whether ASCII-only or Unicode letters are intended.
